result: Reciprocal GABAergic inhibition between SACs is abolished in Slc32a1 KO mice. In control mice, reciprocal inhibition was detected in 9/9 pairs with mean peak amplitude 16.4 ± 2.8 pA, while no evoked IPSCs were detected in Slc32a1 KO mice (n=9 pairs).
evaluation: Claims C16 and C17 are directly supported by paired electrophysiological recordings (Figure 1D-E) showing complete loss of reciprocal SAC-SAC inhibition in Slc32a1 KO mice. The data include appropriate sample sizes and controls, with clear quantification of IPSC amplitudes.

result: In Slc32a1 KO mice with simple moving bar stimuli, On SAC direction selectivity is preserved while Off SAC direction selectivity is slightly enhanced due to decreased centripetal responses. This demonstrates that reciprocal SAC-SAC inhibition is not required for On SAC direction selectivity under these conditions.
evaluation: Claims C20-C23 and C26 are supported by calcium imaging data (Figure 2) showing quantitative DSI and vector sum measurements. The statistical analyses are appropriate, with sufficient sample sizes (n=86 control On SACs, n=20 KO On SACs, n=35 control Off SACs, n=33 KO Off SACs). The conclusion is directly supported by the data.

result: Adding GABAA receptor antagonist SR95531 to Slc32a1 KO retinas reduces direction selectivity in both On and Off SACs, indicating a role for GABAergic inhibition from non-SAC amacrine cells.
evaluation: Claims C24-C25 are supported by pharmacological experiments (Figure 2D-G) with appropriate controls. Since SAC-SAC inhibition is already absent in Slc32a1 KO mice, the effect of SR95531 can be attributed to non-SAC sources. Sample sizes are adequate (n=14 On SACs, n=11 Off SACs).

result: GABAergic inputs onto SACs are abolished in Gabra2 KO mice, as demonstrated by elimination of spontaneous IPSCs and absence of evoked IPSCs in paired recordings.
evaluation: Claims C30-C31 are supported by electrophysiological data (Figure 3B-D) showing complete loss of spontaneous IPSCs (control: 0.28 ± 0.07 Hz, n=18; KO: 0.02 ± 0.04 Hz, n=16, p<0.0005) and no evoked IPSCs in paired recordings (n=10 pairs). The genetic manipulation successfully eliminated functional GABAA receptors in SACs.

result: In Gabra2 KO mice, the asymmetric wiring pattern of GABAergic and cholinergic inputs from SACs to pDSGCs remains unchanged, and glutamatergic inputs to pDSGCs are unaltered, indicating no detectable developmental compensation in the direction selective circuit.
evaluation: Claims C32-C35 and C63 are supported by paired recording experiments (Figure 3E-G) showing preserved asymmetric GABAergic inputs (null vs preferred side), unchanged cholinergic transmission, and similar EPSC amplitudes between control and KO groups. This validates the genetic approach and rules out major developmental compensations.

result: Off SACs in Gabra2 KO mice display significantly increased centripetal-direction responses and reduced direction selectivity during simple moving bar stimuli, demonstrating that direct GABAergic inputs from non-SAC amacrine cells are required for Off SAC centrifugal direction selectivity.
evaluation: Claims C36-C38 and C68 are supported by calcium imaging data (Figure 4) with adequate sample sizes (control n=35 cells, KO n=67 cells). The DSI and vector sum values show statistically significant reductions in KO mice (p<0.0005). The conclusion is strengthened by comparison with Slc32a1 KO results, which showed enhanced Off SAC selectivity.

result: On SACs in Gabra2 KO mice exhibit normal centrifugal direction selectivity during simple moving bar stimuli, indicating that direct GABAergic inputs onto On SACs are not required for direction selectivity under these conditions.
evaluation: Claims C39-C40 and C67 are supported by calcium imaging data (Figure 4) showing no significant difference in DSI or vector sum between control and KO On SACs (control n=86, KO n=124, p>0.2). This is consistent with the Slc32a1 KO results and suggests other mechanisms maintain On SAC direction selectivity.

result: Bath application of SR95531 reduces direction selectivity of On SACs in Gabra2 KO mice, suggesting presynaptic inhibition onto bipolar cells contributes to On SAC direction selectivity.
evaluation: Claims C41-C42 are supported by pharmacological data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) showing significant reduction in DSI after SR95531 application (n=13 cells, p<0.005). Since direct GABAergic inputs onto SACs are already absent in Gabra2 KO mice, the effect must be mediated by presynaptic inhibition onto bipolar cells.

result: In Gabra2 KO mice, the Off component of inhibitory inputs onto pDSGCs shows reduced direction selectivity while the On component remains normal, demonstrating that GABAergic inputs onto Off SACs are required for directionally tuned inhibition in the Off pathway.
evaluation: Claims C43-C46 are supported by voltage clamp recordings (Figure 5) with adequate sample sizes (control n=32, KO n=33). The Off component shows significant reductions in both DSI and charge transfer (p<0.01), while On component shows no significant change. This directly links Off SAC direction selectivity to DSGC inhibitory inputs.

result: The Off component of pDSGC spiking activity shows reduced direction selectivity in Gabra2 KO mice with both bright and dark moving bars, while On responses remain normal. This demonstrates that lateral inhibition onto Off SACs is functionally relevant for DSGC output.
evaluation: Claims C47-C51 are supported by loose-patch recordings (Figure 6) with adequate sample sizes (bright bar: control n=33, KO n=37; dark bar: control n=19, KO n=20). The Off component shows significant reductions in DSI and vector sum (p<0.005) regardless of stimulus polarity, while On responses are preserved. This validates the functional impact on retinal output.

result: With flickering checkerboard backgrounds, On pathway direction selectivity is significantly reduced in Gabra2 KO mice while remaining normal with homogeneous backgrounds at matched contrast and illuminance. This demonstrates that lateral inhibition onto On SACs is recruited under noisy background conditions.
evaluation: Claims C52-C55, C59, and C62 are supported by loose-patch recordings (Figure 7A-D) showing stimulus-dependent recruitment of lateral inhibition. The control experiments varying contrast and illuminance (Figure 7D) rule out these factors as explanations, supporting the conclusion that background noise is the critical factor. Sample sizes are adequate (n=12-18 cells).

result: At various illuminance and contrast levels with homogeneous backgrounds, On pathway direction selectivity remains normal in Gabra2 KO mice while Off pathway selectivity is consistently reduced, demonstrating that the impaired On pathway selectivity with flickering backgrounds is not due to changes in contrast or illuminance.
evaluation: Claims C56-C58 are supported by systematic experiments (Figure 7D) testing multiple conditions. The data show consistent Off pathway deficits and preserved On pathway function across all tested conditions, providing strong evidence that background noise rather than contrast or illuminance is the critical factor.

result: Lateral inhibition from non-SAC amacrine cells onto Off SACs is required for optimal direction selectivity of the Off pathway.
evaluation: Claims C3 and C60 represent the main conclusion for the Off pathway, supported by converging evidence from SAC calcium imaging (C36-C38), DSGC inhibitory inputs (C44, C46), and DSGC spiking responses (C47, C49, C51) in Gabra2 KO mice. The conclusion is well-supported across multiple levels of the circuit.

result: Lateral inhibition onto On SACs is not necessary for direction selectivity with homogeneous backgrounds but is required with noisy backgrounds, demonstrating that distinct inhibitory mechanisms are recruited under different visual conditions.
evaluation: Claims C4-C6 and C61 represent the main conclusions for the On pathway, supported by the differential effects observed with simple bar stimuli (C39-C40) versus flickering checkerboard backgrounds (C54-C55). The systematic control experiments (C56-C58) strengthen this conclusion by ruling out alternative explanations.

result: The direction selective circuitry consists of distinct mechanisms in On and Off sublaminae, with GABAergic inhibition onto SACs having multiple facets engaged differently during processing of positive- and negative-contrast motion.
evaluation: Claims C70-C71 are supported by the differential effects observed in On versus Off pathways across both Slc32a1 KO and Gabra2 KO mice. The data consistently show pathway-specific requirements for lateral inhibition, supporting the conclusion that the circuitry is not simply mirrored between sublaminae.

result: The authors propose that lateral inhibition onto On SACs safeguards direction selectivity against noisy environments by being recruited when bipolar cells are more activated by background noise, creating a 'primed' state for the inhibitory network.
evaluation: Claims C72-C76 are mechanistic hypotheses proposed to explain the experimental observations but lack direct experimental validation. While the hypotheses are reasonable and consistent with known circuit properties, they remain speculative. Direct measurements of bipolar cell activity or amacrine cell activation states under different background conditions would be needed to support these claims.

result: Direction selectivity of On-Off DSGC spiking decreases when SAC centrifugal preference is reduced, demonstrating that inhibitory mechanisms contributing to SAC direction selectivity are functionally relevant for signals relayed from retina to brain.
evaluation: Claims C84-C85 are supported by the correlated reductions in SAC direction selectivity (C36-C37) and DSGC spiking responses (C47, C51) in Gabra2 KO mice. This establishes the functional relevance of the circuit mechanisms studied, though the claim could be strengthened with more direct causal manipulations.

result: The early development of retinal direction selectivity is highly resistant to changes in neural activity, though visual experience can refine preferred direction clustering after direction selectivity is established. pDSGCs in both KO lines remain tuned to the posterior direction.
evaluation: Claims C64-C66 are supported by citations to multiple previous studies and the observation that pDSGCs maintain posterior tuning in both KO lines. However, C64 relies primarily on prior work rather than new data from this study. The lack of developmental compensation (C63) provides additional support.

result: The manuscript establishes the anatomical and functional organization of the retinal direction selective circuit, including SAC properties, DSGC connectivity, and sources of lateral inhibition onto SACs.
evaluation: Claims C1-C2 and C7-C15 describe established knowledge in the field, supported by multiple citations to prior work and illustrated in Figure 1. These claims provide essential background context but do not represent novel findings from this study.

result: Additional neural mechanisms are recruited when visual stimuli more closely resemble natural viewing conditions, while simpler stimuli may not reveal the functional significance of these mechanisms. This principle has been observed in both retina and visual cortex.
evaluation: Claims C77-C79 are supported by citations to previous studies and are consistent with the findings of this manuscript. The comparison to visual cortex (C79) provides a useful analogy. However, these represent general principles rather than specific findings from this study.

result: The genetic approach of eliminating GABAA receptors from SACs while preserving neurotransmitter release overcomes limitations of pharmacological approaches, allowing determination of the role of GABAergic inputs onto SACs in DSGC output.
evaluation: Claims C80-C83 describe the methodological advantages of the genetic approach used in this study. The logic is sound and the approach is validated by the preservation of SAC-DSGC connections (C32-C35). This represents an important methodological contribution.

result: The manuscript describes methodological details including the response properties of On and Off SACs to moving bars, age ranges of mice used, and visual stimulus parameters.
evaluation: Claims C18-C19 and C86-C89 are methodological details directly stated in the manuscript. These are adequately documented and support the reproducibility of the experiments.

result: Gabra2 colocalizes with SAC dendrites and is important for direction selectivity. Wide-field amacrine cells synapse onto proximal dendrites of Off SACs and contribute ~8% of inhibitory synapses onto Off SACs.
evaluation: Claims C28-C29 and C69 are supported by citations to prior work (Brandstätter et al., 1995; Auferkorte et al., 2012; Ding et al., 2016). These provide important context for the genetic manipulation and interpretation of results, though they do not represent novel findings from this study.
